chunks: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): A man had a female slave whom he had sexual relations with; she died or he sold her, then afterwards he acquired her mother. Is it permissible for him to marry her? He wrote: It is not permissible for him.

key_terms.يَطَؤُهَا: He has sexual relations with her

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a man to marry the mother of a female slave he previously had relations with after she dies or is sold?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Istibsar, Imam al-Hassan al-Muqtadi (AS) rules that a man is prohibited from marrying the mother of a female slave (ummu al-walad) with whom he has had sexual relations, even after her death or sale. This ruling highlights the permanence of the 'mahram' relationship established by consummation, preventing marriage to the mother to avoid confusion in lineage and family structure, a principle consistent with the treatment of free women in Shia jurisprudence.
